note: Chapter presets are research-informed staging hypotheses, not exact historical weather records. Mood/weather/season/time presets are partial layers.

presets.label: 01 · A family and a promise
presets.place: Vermont and West Lebanon New Hampshire
presets.note: Vermont/New Hampshire winter. The room is the whole world: low child eye height, firelight, deep blue window, snow at the glass. No heroic key light; the father's hand is the brightest thing in frame.

presets.label: 02 · Many voices in Palmyra
presets.weather: volcanic cold, low cloud, then revival heat
presets.note: The Year Without a Summer is the environmental fact behind the chapter. Start with a cold, veiled 1816 sky and grey-green fields; let the later revival meetings warm slightly, but never into a postcard summer.
tags: volcanic cold, low cloud, then revival heat

presets.label: 03 · The Sacred Grove
presets.note: Joseph Smith—History 1:14 gives the only secure weather sentence in the whole campaign: a beautiful, clear morning early in the spring of 1820. Build the grove as a cathedral of green and gold, then let the pillar of light out-brighten the sun.

presets.label: 04 · Moroni in the night
presets.note: The visit is at night, and 21 September 1823 was close to full moon. Let blue moonlight define the room, then let the messenger's light become the key: 'lighter than at noonday' (JS-H 1:30). The palette moves from indigo to silver-white.

presets.label: 05 · The hill and the years of preparation
presets.shortLabel: The hill and the years of preparation
presets.place: The hill near Manchester and the Smith home
presets.note: The hill chapters are years of return visits; use a low September sun, ground mist, and a cool blue shadow side. Gold on the hilltop, not a warm hearth.

presets.label: 06 · Emma and the entrusted record
presets.note: A hand-to-hand journey with a guarded record. Wet brown roads, slate sky, one warm lantern; keep faces half-lit and the horizon closed in.

presets.label: 07 · Harmony and the lost manuscript
presets.note: Harmony in summer is humid and close. Use a green-gold exterior and a dim interior lit by one window; the lost manuscript chapter should feel airless rather than rainy.

presets.label: 08 · Oliver and the work of translation
presets.shortLabel: Oliver and the work of translation
presets.place: Harmony and the Whitmer farm in Fayette
presets.note: April to June in Harmony and Fayette: new leaves, clean light, work that fills the frame. Let the palette be fresher and higher-key than the lost-manuscript chapter.

presets.label: 09 · Authority beside the river
presets.note: The Susquehanna in May is high, cold, and silver. Use a pale sky, river mist, and a cool key with warm faces; the water should be the brightest horizontal band.

presets.label: 10 · Witnesses and the printed book
presets.note: Witnesses and the printed book sit at the turn from winter to spring in western New York. Grey snowmelt, warm ink and paper, a low sun through cloud. The book is the colour event.

presets.label: 11 · The Church and the first New York congregations
presets.shortLabel: The Church and the first New York congregations
presets.place: Fayette Colesville and the New York settlements
presets.note: Fayette and Colesville in 1830: orchards, mud, new grass, a community finding its feet. Use a lower, warmer afternoon key than the Fayette translation scenes.

presets.label: 12 · Gathering to Ohio
presets.note: Kirtland's first gathering: northeast Ohio autumn, hard blue sky, yellow leaves, white frame buildings. Use a clean, cool shadow side against warm wood.

presets.label: 13 · A place for Zion
presets.weather: hot, humid, storm on the horizon
presets.note: Independence in summer is hot, wet, and enormous. Tallgrass green, bleached dust, a bruised storm wall on the horizon; the light should feel too large for the people in it.
tags: hot, humid, storm on the horizon

presets.label: 14 · The vision of eternity
presets.note: The February 1832 vision in Hiram: a winter night room, ordinary oil light, then a glory that makes the lamp irrelevant. Keep the room dark enough for the vision to read.

presets.label: 15 · The night in Hiram
presets.note: The mob attack at Hiram is a night of cold air, lanterns, firearms, tar, and feathers. Use a cold blue exterior, a warm violent burst at the door, and desaturated skin. Do not make it picturesque.

presets.label: N1 · Great buildings, an open conversation
presets.place: Lower Manhattan, New York City · Pearl Street House and streets
presets.note: Lower Manhattan in October 1832: early gaslight, wet stone, coal smoke, the Pearl Street house. Use warm gas pools inside a blue-grey street; the city should feel newly, unevenly lit.

presets.label: 16 · Learning to be a people
presets.note: The Whitney store and school of the prophets: plain, bright, utilitarian. Whitewash, brown wood, green outside; light should be even and legible, not mystical.

presets.label: 17 · Letters from the driven Saints
presets.place: Kirtland with news from Jackson County
presets.note: Kirtland hears of the Jackson County expulsions. Use a warm interior against a cold blue window; the letter paper is the brightest object, the faces are tired.

presets.label: 18 · Zion's Camp
presets.place: The road from Ohio to Missouri
presets.note: Zion's Camp across Ohio, Indiana, and Missouri: sun-bleached dust, sudden prairie storms, tired animals. Use a wide, low-contrast dusty key and a bruised sky; rain only as a passing wall.

presets.label: 19 · A ministry for the world
presets.note: 1835 Kirtland: the Twelve and Seventy are called; the town is growing. High summer light, white limestone, deep green; a public, outdoor brightness.

presets.label: 20 · The Kirtland Temple
presets.note: Kirtland Temple, 27 March–3 April 1836. The dedication was an early-morning gathering in a cold Ohio spring. Use pale gold sun through high windows, cold blue shadow, and a distinct supernatural layer for the day of Pentecost.

presets.label: 21 · Faith in a time of loss
presets.shortLabel: Faith in a time of loss
presets.note: Kirtland 1837–38: financial collapse, leaving, snow. Use a bleached grey palette, low contrast, cold hands; the warm windows are few and far between.

presets.label: 22 · Far West and the Missouri conflict
presets.shortLabel: Far West and the Missouri conflict
presets.note: Far West and northern Missouri in 1838: armed tension, burnt-out farms, autumn smoke. Use a dirty amber key, low grey cloud, and deep red-brown shadows; avoid a clean heroic battlefield look.

presets.label: 23 · Liberty Jail
presets.note: Liberty Jail, winter 1838–39: cold stone, poor food, a low cellar light. Keep the frame almost monochrome blue-grey, with one candle-warm pool on hands and paper. The voice of the chapter is hope inside a cold cell.

presets.label: 24 · Nauvoo rises by the river
presets.place: Commerce and Nauvoo Illinois with a Washington journey
presets.note: Nauvoo rising by the Mississippi: wet spring ground, limestone and brick, river light. Use broad, clean daylight with a cool river band and warm masonry.

presets.label: 25 · Two days in the Nauvoo Lodge
presets.shortLabel: Two days in the Nauvoo Lodge
presets.place: The upper floor of the Red Brick Store
presets.note: The Red Brick Store upper room, 15–16 March 1842: oil lamps, washing, anointing, a small enclosed world. Use warm lamp pools against deep brown shadow; almost no sky.

presets.label: 26 · Relief covenant and eternal family
presets.note: Nauvoo 1842–43: Relief Society, family, politics, heat. Use a lush but heavy green, brick red, Mississippi haze; the beauty should have weight.

presets.label: B1 · Walker Lewis: a room for a great question
presets.shortLabel: Walker Lewis: a room for a great question
presets.place: Lowell, Massachusetts · interpretive barbershop and mill-town street
presets.note: Lowell, Massachusetts, c. 1843–44: brick mills, coal smoke, immigrant streets, a barbershop interior. Use soot-softened light, brick red, slate blue, and one warm interior pool. Elijah Able and Jane Manning deserve portrait lighting, not silhouette.

presets.label: 27 · A voice in the republic
presets.dateLabel: January to February 1844; campaign resumes after April 7
presets.note: Nauvoo, January–February 1844: a presidential campaign in winter. Use newsprint white, ink black, cold blue, and one red accent; the light is public and exposed.

presets.label: 28 · The King Follett memorial discourse
presets.place: Nauvoo conference and later civic gatherings
presets.dateLabel: April 7, 1844; separate campaign continuation April to June
presets.note: The King Follett discourse, 7 April 1844, outdoors before a large crowd. No reliable daily weather record was located, so stage it as a bright, cool spring morning: new leaves, hard sunlight, wind. The sermon's scale needs a big sky.

presets.label: 29 · The city council and the road to Carthage
presets.shortLabel: The city council and the road to Carthage
presets.note: Nauvoo to Carthage, June 1844. The road should be bleached and dusty, the river a hot mirror, the sky too wide. This chapter hands the player to the jail; it should already feel like the light is draining.

presets.label: 30 · Carthage · The Martyrdom
presets.place: The upper room of Carthage Jail
presets.confidence: reported: room very hot; late afternoon; no torchlit-night claim
presets.note: Carthage, 27 June 1844, about 5 p.m. Period accounts say the upstairs room became very hot and the men opened the windows; the mob came in late afternoon with painted faces and firearms. Stage the historical preset as bleached pastoral green, dusty gold sun, grey-green shadow, and a slow desaturation toward ash. Torches/pitchforks belong only to the clearly labelled stylised nightmare preset.

presets.label: 30 · Carthage — torchlit nightmare (stylised)
presets.confidence: stylised — not a historical weather claim
presets.note: A deliberately non-historical nightmare version for comparison: the same pastoral green world under a black storm sky, lit by torches and muzzle flashes. Period accounts place the attack in late afternoon and mention painted faces and firearms; torches and pitchforks are symbolic staging, not documented equipment. Keep the label visible whenever this preset is used.

presets.label: 31 · Beyond the veil
presets.note: The spirit-world interval is designed, not historical. Use a pearl-and-indigo twilight, soft vertical light, no hard sun, and a horizon that refuses to resolve.

presets.label: 32 · A world entrusted to love
presets.place: Celestial space and a new living world
presets.dateLabel: A visionary far future beyond a specified earthly date
presets.note: Celestial space and the new world: no earthly weather. Use a high-key gold/rose/cyan palette, long soft bloom, and a sky that reads as light rather than atmosphere.

presets.label: E1 · The garden before the years
presets.place: One fictional mission landscape across changing eras
presets.note: Eden is an imagined mission landscape. Use saturated young green, warm mist, enormous soft sun, and a world without dust or damage.

presets.label: E2 · Questions in the nineteenth century
presets.place: One fictional mission landscape across changing eras
presets.dateLabel: Salt Lake City after 1847 · fictional reflection
presets.note: Salt Lake City after 1847, used as a fictional reflection. High desert light: hard sun, sage and ochre, a blue that goes almost black at zenith, mountains as a cool wall.

presets.label: E3 · A doorstep in 1955
presets.place: One fictional mission landscape across changing eras
presets.note: A 1955 doorstep: postwar suburb, autumn leaves, a low sun through elm trees, a car in the drive. Use Kodachrome warmth with one wrong cool shadow; nostalgia should be slightly too clean.

presets.label: E4 · The family archive
presets.place: One fictional mission landscape across changing eras
presets.note: 1994 family archive: fluorescent tubes, beige carpet, a CRT, paper. Use flat greenish light, low contrast, and one warm desk lamp; the past is stored under office lighting.

presets.label: E5 · The shared water
presets.place: One fictional mission landscape across changing eras
presets.note: 2026 shared water: a near-future Nauvoo under climate stress. Use harsh white sun, bleached concrete, a low river, and a storm that may or may not break; keep hope in the people, not the sky.

presets.label: E6 · The desert after the fire
presets.place: One fictional mission landscape across changing eras
presets.note: The desert after the fire: an imagined nuclear aftermath. Use a red-black sky, falling ash, ember light, and no green; the palette is charcoal, rust, and bone.

presets.label: E7 · The closed archive
presets.place: One fictional mission landscape across changing eras
presets.dateLabel: An imagined future of guarded knowledge
presets.note: The closed archive: a future of guarded knowledge. Use cold fluorescent strips, grey-green concrete, deep black outside the glass, and one screen-blue glow. The light should feel like surveillance.

presets.label: E8 · Zion is a welcome
presets.place: One fictional mission landscape across changing eras
presets.note: Zion is a welcome: an imagined open future. Use a high, clean morning, gold-green, water, and a horizon full of doors; the brightest scene in the game, but not white-out.
